note: Clean pass, one caveat about the English columns. item_text is the administered Indonesian, taken verbatim from the header of the raw-text column that sits immediately left of each coded column in the PLOS S1 workbook (10.1371/journal.pone.0280313.s001); the coded column names ARE the IRW item codes, so no positional inference. The left-neighbour pairing was proved rather than assumed: for all 28 items the label values in the text column cross-tabulate one-to-one with the integers in the code column over all 390 rows (e.g. SD_1: Tidak pernah=1 (20), Kadang-kadang=2 (207), Cukup sering=3 (117), Sangat sering=4 (44); H_2: 153/190/38/7), so option_text->resp is decisive too. item_text_translated is Carver's own English for the correspondingly numbered Brief COPE item (the workbook reproduces Carver's 1-28 order exactly), i.e. a parallel official version, not a word-for-word back-translation of the Indonesian. option_text_translated (Never/Sometimes/Quite often/Very often) is IRW's translation of the study's own Indonesian frequency anchors -- the study administered frequency anchors, not Carver's 'I haven't been doing this at all'..'a lot', so no published English for them exists. instructions and section_prompt are blank: the workbook carries no instruction row and the paper does not quote the administered Indonesian instructions; Carver's English instructions are surgery-specific and were not shipped. Rights: Carver's own page (psy.miami.edu/faculty/ccarver/brief-cope.html) states 'You are welcome to use all scales of the Brief COPE, or to choose selected scales for use' and 'Feel free as well to adapt the language for whatever time scale you are interested in' -- no fee, no NC/ND, no redistribution bar; the site's generic 'Copyright: 2026 University of Miami' footer is a bare notice, not a reserved right, so silence-is-permission applies. Step 3b: instrument confirmed -- 28 items, 14 two-item subscales, 1-4 scoring, matching the paper's Methods description of the Brief COPE.

PASS with three caveats, none blocking. (1) ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: the MPILMBB sample is 194 native German-speaking participants scanned at MPI-CBS/University of Leipzig, and the paper states a German version for essentially every other instrument it describes (AMAS, ASR, BIS/BAS, BP, SCS, ESS, S-D-MW ...). It never states the administered language of the Short-NYC-Q specifically, and no German wording exists anywhere in the deposit or the paper's supplements -- SNYCQ.json (Dataverse datafile 3322525, 86 entries) contains 0 German characters, sdata2018307-s2.docx (the code description supplement) contains 1 in the whole file and none in any SNYCQ entry, and sdata2018307-s4.docx prints even the MPI MRI safety questionnaire in English. So the deposit's English ships in the base fields with the _translated columns empty, language=German, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. If the Short-NYC-Q was in fact administered in English (Smallwood is a co-author and the instrument is his group's), language=German is the wrong call and the fallback is unnecessary -- the paper does not settle it either way. (2) VERBATIM, INCLUDING ARTIFACTS: item_text is copied exactly from the SNYCQ.json Description first lines and three punctuation artifacts are shipped uncorrected rather than silently normalised -- 'I thought about future events..' (double period), 'I thought about something positive' (no terminal period, unlike the other 11), and 'my present environment/ surrounding.' (space after the slash). The item CODE typo 'surrpundings' is the join key and is untouched. (3) INSTRUCTIONS BLANK BY DESIGN: no participant-facing instruction text is published. The paper's own description of the response format ('The questions can be rated using a digital format of a scale bar, with an answer resolution of 5% increments (0%="describes my thoughts not at all"- 100%="describes my thoughts completely)') is third-person, and its 5%-increment claim is contradicted by the live data (resp takes 170 distinct values on a ~0.6579 = 100/152 grid, not 21 values on a 5-point grid), so it is not shipped as instructions; only its two endpoint anchors are shipped, as option_text on resp=0 and resp=100. (4) RESP AXIS: resp is a continuous 0-100 VAS, so option_text is blank (NA) for the other 168 levels -- the source publishes no label for any interior point and none was invented. Rows are per item x the levels that item's own respondents used (1660 rows), reproduced from the source TSV and confirmed against irw::irw_table_sets(per_item=TRUE): all 12 items match on n (1189-1192) and on n_resp_levels (123-148) exactly.

PASS with caveats. Item codes EQ and EQ2 each cover two literal wordings under the study's counterbalanced design -- the name question in name-first (NC) trials and the color question in color-first (CN) trials (the trial's order is in cov_pattern) -- so both are given in item_text with the condition named in brackets; AQ, AQ2 and AQ3 share one identical question ("What about this?") and are distinguished only by their position in the fixed EQ/AQ/EQ2/AQ2/AQ3 sequence, not by wording. Also: option_text carries the paper's English scoring labels correct/incorrect rather than administered wording (children answered openly, read no options), so option_text_translated is blank while language=Chinese; instructions and section_prompt are blank because the paper publishes no verbatim instruction text.

STEP 3b INSTRUMENT MISMATCH (dictionary correction owed). The IRW Data Dictionary Description for merlo2025_eet reads "Educational Engagement with Technology scale - EET (29 items); Italian university students". Both halves are wrong. EET in this deposit is the study's EVENING EATING BEHAVIOUR questionnaire: the deposit's own data dictionary (Final-dataset-grid.csv) gives every EET_nn the stem "Con che frequenza di solito consumi uno o piu degli alimenti elencati a cena o prima di andare a dormire:" followed by a food (Anacardi, Aragosta, Cacao, ... Uova), and the paper's section 3.2.2 "Evening eating behaviour (EET)" describes exactly this - a list of 28 tryptophan-rich foods rated for evening consumption frequency. Technology use is a DIFFERENT block in the same file (TECH_01..TECH_24), which data/merlo2025_engagement.py deliberately excludes as non-ordinal. The sample is also 1065 SECONDARY SCHOOL students (mean age 15.95, SD 1.46), not university students. Suggested Description: "Evening eating behaviour questionnaire - EET (29 items: 28 tryptophan-rich foods + 1 attention check); Italian secondary school students; N=1065; 1-6 frequency Likert". CAVEATS ON THE SHIPPED TEXT: (1) EET_17 is not a food - it is an embedded attention check, "Seleziona la risposta Mai" (select the answer "Never"), and 1034/1065 respondents complied; correct_response is left blank because a frequency scale has no key, but consumers pooling the 29 items into a diet score should drop EET_17. (2) The deposit's data dictionary has had its apostrophes and commas flattened to spaces by whatever exported it, so the shipped Italian reads "Crusca d avena", "Kellogg s All Bran" and "Halibut detto anche pesce ippoglosso"; the wording is verbatim, the punctuation is not restored. (3) The Italian response anchors were never published - option_text carries the authors' own English (never/rarely/sometimes/often/almost always/always) while item_text carries the administered Italian.
